{{Quote|Command unit retrieved. Uploading memory... Destroy all the Jedi... di...|Gold MagnaGuard upon reactivating|<ref name="ROTS GBA/DS" />}}
This '''MagnaGuard''', alongside a [[Unidentified IG-100 MagnaGuard (Green)|green counterpart]], were present alongside a few other [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]]-aligned [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] in the [[Cave/Legends|caves]] of [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]]. However, several of the [[Droid/Legends|droids]] ended up devoured by [[Nos monster/Legends|Nos monsters]]. The attack was also such that both [[IG-100 MagnaGuard/Legends|IG-100 MagnaGuards]] were temporarily deactivated while subtly entering repair mode due to their containing a self-repair unit.

By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the later parts of the [[Battle of Utapau/Legends|Battle of Utapau]], [[General/Legends|General]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], who had been forced to flee into the caves due to [[Gender/Legends|his]] [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] [[Order 66/Legends|turning against him]], encountered the two, also noting the droids present were devoured. The [[Gold/Legends|gold]] [[Color/Legends|colored]] one was the first to reactivate, and upon rebooting its command unit's memory, remembered that it's primary objective was to destroy all the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], and possessed a slight stutter. He then fought the two, eventually destroying them quickly after learning of their self-repair function.

==Behind the scenes==
This IG-100 MagnaGuard, alongside its green counterpart, acted as the third boss overall in Obi-Wan Kenobi's storyline in the GBA and Nintendo DS versions of the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|video game adaptation]] of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]
